label: <DEL> step of long sequences, first token r (or m/i/k/t/p/2/g/h/j)
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step (97.6% of activation mass; never in the copy phase), at the point where the model must output original token 0. It needs long sequences: essentially silent for L<=5, weak for L=6-7, most mass at L=8-9. Which first token is about to be recalled sets both whether it fires and how strongly: first token r is the strongest (31% of mass, 72% firing rate at L>=7 delimiters; every top example starts with r), followed by m, i, k, t, p, 2, g. A small leftover (2.4% of mass) fires weakly on the last one or two original tokens of L=8-9 sequences. It does not fire on short sequences, on copy steps, or reliably on any one first token, and many long-sequence delimiters with other first tokens stay silent. Precision is limited because the first-token dependence is graded, not a clean set.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: r, m, k, i, t, p; least: n, f, c, q) and the previous input (most: p, g, 3, j, u, b; least: c, l, x, n); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, t=7, L=9 & t=8.
